title: Modern CPU Microarchitecture
description: How a core finds independent work: prediction, renaming, out-of-order issue, and the memory system that has to stay honest across cores.

sourceReferences.title: MIT 6.823 Computer System Architecture
sourceReferences.notes: Superscalar/VLIW/vector/threads after ISA and caches. Multiprocessors and memory models last.

sourceReferences.title: Stanford CS149
sourceReferences.notes: Coherence and consistency after the core is thinkable, not as GPU week-one.

sourceReferences.title: Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual
sourceReferences.notes: Store buffers, serializing ops, and the x86 ordering model as architectural facts.

sourceReferences.title: Arm Architecture Reference Manual
sourceReferences.notes: Relaxed default ordering and explicit barriers, after coherence is thinkable.

modules.title: Speculating control
modules.blurb: Prediction so the pipeline stays full.

modules.title: Renaming and out-of-order
modules.blurb: Names, the ROB, and retiring in program order.
learningObjectives: Explain why architectural names are too few

concepts.name: Branch prediction
concepts.summary: Guessing control flow so the pipeline stays full.
objectives: Separate direction prediction from target prediction
Say what a mispredict costs in a full pipeline

concepts.name: Branch target buffers
concepts.summary: Caching where a branch went last time, not just taken/not-taken.
objectives: State that a BTB caches a fetch redirect address, not a taken bit
Explain why a late-discovered taken branch still costs a bubble

concepts.name: Predictor types
concepts.summary: Local, global, and TAGE-style predictors and why they exist.
objectives: Contrast local history with global or TAGE-style correlation
Explain why one history length is not enough

concepts.name: Return address stacks
concepts.summary: Special-casing CALL/RET so returns do not pollute the BTB.
objectives: Explain how CALL/RET uses a LIFO stack of return PCs
Diagnose overflow and why kernels stuff or flush the RAS

concepts.name: Issue width
concepts.summary: How many operations a cycle can start if they are ready.
objectives: Define issue width as how many ready ops can start in one cycle
Contrast width with the supply of independent work

concepts.name: Register renaming
concepts.summary: Mapping architectural names onto a larger physical file.
objectives: Separate false WAW/WAR name conflicts from true RAW edges
Treat an architectural register as a pointer into a larger physical file

concepts.name: Reorder buffers
concepts.summary: Retiring out-of-order work in program order.
objectives: State in-order allocate and commit around out-of-order execute
Explain why stores wait for commit before becoming globally visible

concepts.name: Out-of-order scheduling
concepts.summary: Issuing ready work, not the next instruction in program order.
objectives: Explain issuing ready work rather than the next program-order instruction
Name what a scheduler entry is waiting on

concepts.name: Wakeup and select
concepts.summary: Broadcasting completions and picking the next ready ops.
objectives: Describe wakeup as broadcasting a completion to waiting ops
Describe select as choosing which ready ops occupy issue slots

concepts.name: Precise exceptions
concepts.summary: The illusion that nothing after the faulting instruction happened.
objectives: State the illusion that nothing after the faulting instruction happened
Explain how a ROB flush restores architectural state

concepts.name: Simultaneous multithreading
concepts.summary: Filling issue slots from another thread when this one cannot.
objectives: Explain filling leftover issue slots from another thread
Name the structures two threads typically share

concepts.name: Load/store queues
concepts.summary: Tracking memory ops so they can complete without lying about order.
objectives: Say why memory ops need their own queues besides the ROB
Track a store so a later load can see it without going to cache

concepts.name: Memory disambiguation
concepts.summary: Guessing that a load does not overlap an earlier store.
objectives: State what it means to guess that a load does not overlap an earlier store
Predict the recovery when the dependence guess is wrong

concepts.name: Speculative loads
concepts.summary: Starting a load before you know you should.
objectives: Explain starting a load before control or dependence is known
Name what must be undone if the load should not have happened

concepts.name: Store buffers
concepts.summary: Letting the core retire a store before memory has it.
objectives: Say why a store buffer lets the core retire a store before memory has it
Contrast store-buffer forwarding with waiting for the cache

concepts.name: Miss-status holding registers
concepts.summary: Outstanding misses as first-class state.
objectives: Treat an outstanding miss as first-class state
Explain merging a second miss to the same line

concepts.name: Hardware prefetch
concepts.summary: Starting the next line because the past looked sequential.
objectives: Explain starting the next line because the past looked sequential
Name a case where prefetch hurts

concepts.name: Inclusion and exclusivity
concepts.summary: Whether a line in L1 must also live in L2.
objectives: State what inclusion requires of L2 when a line is in L1
Contrast exclusive hierarchies with inclusive ones

concepts.name: Cache coherency
concepts.summary: Keeping private caches honest across cores.
objectives: State the single-writer / multiple-reader rule for one address
Separate coherence from consistency

concepts.name: MESI-style protocols
concepts.summary: Invalidation as the way two writers do not invent two truths.
objectives: Name what a write to a Shared line must do
Diagnose false sharing as two variables on one line

concepts.name: Snooping versus directories
concepts.summary: Broadcast versus asking a known owner.
objectives: Contrast broadcast snooping with asking a directory
Predict which scales worse as core count grows

concepts.name: Memory consistency
concepts.summary: What stores another core is allowed to see, and when.
objectives: Define what stores another core is allowed to see and when
Explain why coherence alone does not pick a memory model

concepts.name: TSO and relaxed models
concepts.summary: Why x86 feels stronger than a phone core.
objectives: Contrast TSO store-load reordering with a weaker model
Say why a fence exists

concepts.name: SIMD and vectors
concepts.summary: One instruction, many packed elements, no implicit divergence.
objectives: Define SIMD as one instruction on packed elements you named
Contrast packed SIMD with a scalar data-parallel loop

concepts.name: VLIW as compile-time ILP
concepts.summary: The compiler packs the issue group so the hardware does not have to.
objectives: State that the compiler packs the issue group
Name the trade-off when the compiler guessed wrong about independence

concepts.name: The power wall
concepts.summary: Why frequency stopped being the scaling story.
objectives: Explain why frequency stopped being the scaling story
Relate extra ILP to power and voltage cost

concepts.name: Speculation and side channels
concepts.summary: Transient state that microarchitecture can observe even when architecture cannot.
objectives: Explain that transient state can be observed even when architecture rolls it back
Reason about why a speculative load plus a predictor creates a side channel

concepts.name: Microcode assists
concepts.summary: Complex ops that become little programs inside the core.
objectives: State that some ISA ops become a small internal program
Explain why a microcode assist is not a new architectural instruction
